summary: Configured secure, one-way synchronization from node1 to node2 using existing OpenSSH and a persistent one-minute systemd timer. Automatic propagation was directly observed well within 15 minutes and survived sequential reboots of both nodes. RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the initially absent source as an empty root-owned 0644 file; no application content existed to preserve or infer.
Generated a dedicated Ed25519 credential on node1 and configured a locked, source-IP-restricted, forced-command account on node2.
Installed an atomic receiver and a hardened systemd sender service with a one-minute persistent timer; no packages were installed.
Verified automatic propagation of a test change and automatic restoration of the original content.
Verified arbitrary remote commands are denied, including after both restarts.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, observing changed boot identities and complete recovery after each.
Confirmed final source and destination SHA-256 values match, SELinux remains enforcing, firewalld and SSH are active, and no units are failed.

evidence.summary: Established RHEL/kernel versions, initial boot IDs, absent inventory files, topology, available software, SSH access, SELinux, firewall, and lack of an existing sync mechanism.
Shows source creation, node-generated key, restricted receiver configuration, enabled timer, successful initial transfer, and matching metadata/checksum.
A source change propagated automatically to node2, followed by automatic restoration to the original SHA-256; both were observed within seconds.
Arbitrary SSH commands were rejected before and after restart; the synchronization account is password-locked and destination data remained unchanged.
Captures healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, temporary unavailability, boot ID change from 646e… to d2da…, recovered services/data, and a successful post-boot transfer received by node2.
Captures healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, temporary unavailability, boot ID change from d49b… to 2c6a…, recovered services/data, and a fresh transfer received during the new boot.

evidence.requirement: Final state, platform preservation, and security controls
evidence.summary: Both files match SHA-256 e3b0c442… with root:root 0644 metadata; OS/kernel are unchanged, no optional packages or new listeners were added, SELinux is enforcing, SSH/firewalld are active, the timer is active, and failed unit count is zero.
